tldr: InfiGUIAgent is an MLLM-based GUI agent trained via a two-stage supervised fine-tuning pipeline that enhances both fundamental GUI understanding/grounding and native reasoning abilities (hierarchical and expectation-reflection reasoning), achieving competitive performance on GUI benchmarks.
contributions: A two-stage supervised fine-tuning pipeline to improve both fundamental abilities and advanced reasoning of GUI Agents.
Synthesis of SFT data incorporating hierarchical reasoning and expectation-reflection reasoning, enabling native complex reasoning.
InfiGUIAgent-2B demonstrating competitive performance on multiple GUI benchmarks.
methods: In Stage 1, the authors collected ~1M samples across five categories (GUI understanding, grounding, QA, general knowledge, tool usage) from multiple datasets to train fundamental GUI understanding and instruction grounding. Data was standardized with a [0,1000] coordinate system and a Reference-Augmented Annotation format for spatial grounding. In Stage 2, 45K reasoning-enhanced samples were synthesized from existing trajectories using Qwen2-VL-72B, incorporating hierarchical reasoning (strategic and tactical layers) and expectation-reflection reasoning (expectation generation, action, reflection cycle). The model was continual SFT on Qwen2-VL-2B across 8 A800 80GB GPUs.
results: On ScreenSpot, InfiGUIAgent-2B achieved 76.3% average accuracy, surpassing ShowUI-2B (75.1%) and UGround-7B (73.3%), with per-platform scores of Mobile: 82.8% text / 60.4% icon, Desktop: 78.0% text / 52.0% icon, Web: 72.2% text / 30.0% icon. On AndroidWorld, InfiGUIAgent-2B achieved a 0.09 success rate, outperforming ShowUI-2B (0.07), LLaVA-OV-7B (0.00), and Qwen2-VL-72B (0.05). Experiments used raw screenshots without Set-of-Marks annotations.
limitations: AndroidWorld success rate is only 0.09, indicating limited effectiveness on complex multi-step task automation.
The model does not rely on SoM annotations but this also means it must handle raw screenshots without enhanced visual grounding, potentially limiting performance compared to models using such aids.
No ablation on the individual contribution of hierarchical vs. expectation-reflection reasoning is explicitly reported in the provided text.
